description.narrative:
In March 2020, the Secretariat of the General Federation of Bahrain Trade Unions (GFBTU) held successfully its fourth General Congress. A new leadership was elected and a work plan developed, focussing on enhancing organizing through innovative strategies.
In Febraury 2020, the GFBTU approved the creation of the Migrant Workers Committee - comprising of 13 migrant workers from seven countries (Ethiopia, Cameroon, India, Kenya, Nepal, Philippines and Sri Lanka) to support organizing and protecting migrant workers in Bahrain. From April to May 2020, the GFBTU launched an online questionnaire to assess the impact of COVID-19 on migrant workers (capturing responses from 308 respondents from numerous nationalities). Based on the evidence that many workers (66 per cent) did not receive their owed wages, and many others were facing a humanitarian crisis, the GFBTU allocated internal resources to temporarily provide food and other aid. GFBTU in collaboration of the Indian embassy facilitated access to vaccination for around 3,500 Indian workers in an irregular situation, who by June 2021 had received at least one dose of the vaccine. In February 2021, the GFBTU launched an initiative to strengthen the role of the Migrant Workers' Committee (MWC), as well as a hotline and a lawyer to provide legal support (55 cases during the reporting period). In total, the GFBTU has trained more than 120 (Philippine) migrant workers on the labour law, reached more than 600 (Indian) workers, particularly in the construction and cleaning sectors, with awareness raising campaign on OSH - focussing on heat exhaustion and other heat-related risks. Moreover, GFBTU was actively engaged through meetings with the Minister of Labour and requested intervention to facilitate the vaccination for workers in an irregular situation.
The GFBTU issued a position paper that constitutes its comprehensive vision to reform the labour market, and sustainability of the social insurance and pension funds. The ILO technically supported the General Federation of Bahrain Trade Unions (GFBTU) to develop its new work plan and its vision to reform social security systems and advance social dialogue in Bahrain.
Through ILO technical and financial support, the Migrant Workers Committee organized activities and improved its services to outreach and organize domestic workers. A legal unit was established and offered training and support.
Through the financial support of the FAIRWAY project, and in cooperation with Building and Wood Worker's International (BWI), GFBTU offered technical support to outreach migrant workers in the construction sector and promote social dialogue. An assessment study was conducted and a tripartite meeting was held where constituents agreed on several issues to enhance cooperation.
ILO supported GFBTU to build the capacity of its leaders, through regional webinars/trainings implemented for the Arab Trade Union Organizations in May, June, July and December 2020, and in February, June, and July 2021. The activities focused on the Impact of COVID-19 on workers and the role of trade unions during the crisis.
Furthermore, 17 young GFBTU leaders were trained by ITCILO. Seven participated in the Turin training on Using ILS to achieve Decent Work and Social Justice From June to August 2020. Fice participated in the training on Impact of Austerity Measures on Decent Work and Workers' Organisations from March to April 2021. Five participated in the OSH Academy for Arab Trade Unions.
